thread:
sam: kicking off the release to prod in the 10:00–11:00 change window. linking the backout/runbook here: https://confluence.redwood.com/releases/backout-playbook
lina: thanks — can we confirm the abort triggers we'll use for this canary? quick list please
devon: agreed. propose: 1) sustained 5xx > 1% for 3m 2) p95 latency > 350ms for 5m 3) error spike in core API (auth/response mismatches) 4) any data migration integrity failure
maya: add model-quality regression: if automated eval on canary prompts drops BLEU-like score by >4 points or hallucination rate up by 10% vs baseline -> abort
carol: who has permission to execute the backout? want to avoid finger-pointing during the window
sam: release lead (sam) + oncall (devon) can trigger. ops-bot will record the action. also product-ops must be notified if model rollback happens
devon: escape hatch commands we covered before. copy here for quick access:
```
# quick abort
/deploy abort --release <release-id>
# pin previous image
kubectl -n prod set image deploy/web web=registry.redwood/release:2026-02-18
# immediate traffic cut
kubectl -n prod scale deployment web --replicas=0
``` 
lina: what about version pinning for dependent services? we had an issue last time where worker schema lagged
maya: pinned worker tag is included in release notes. if backout required, we roll both web + worker to previous tags. commands:
```
kubectl -n prod set image deployment/worker worker=registry.redwood/worker:2026-02-18
``` 
sam: ops-bot will post a short checklist when abort is triggered, e.g.:
- announce abort in #eng-oncall and #product
- pin traffic to previous revision
- revert feature flags for rollout
- run sanity smoke on core endpoints
- start postmortem
ops-bot: preflight checks passed for canary: DB migrations: none, schema drift: none, healthchecks: ok
carol: how long do we wait before deciding to backout for degraded metrics? do we tolerate transient spikes
devon: rolling threshold: if metric breach is seen for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets -> hold canary and investigate. if persists for 5 minutes -> abort
lina: can we add a manual hold step before full abort? i.e. pause traffic 50% -> check logs -> then decide
sam: yes. procedure:
1) Hold (scale canary to 0 -> pause new traffic) or set traffic to 50%
2) Triage for 10 minutes (logs, traces, eval harness)
3) If root cause not resolved -> Abort and pin previous
maya: for model regressions specifically, we have an eval harness run triggered by the canary. results should be in the release thread; if fails, abort immediately
carol: note: DB write-path changes are non-trivial — if any write schema change was in release, abort threshold is zero (no partials)
devon: acknowledged. this release has no write schema changes
sam: logging the pin ids here for quick rollback:
- web: registry.redwood/release:2026-02-18
- worker: registry.redwood/worker:2026-02-18
- model: model-v1.14-quant
lina: who will run the post-abort smoke tests? i can run the API checks, devon can run infra checks
devon: i'll run infra + routing checks. sam will validate client-facing happy path
sam: quick reminder for runbook steps (in case of abort):
- run /deploy abort
- pin images (kubectl set image)
- flip feature flags off
- invalidate caches if needed: redis-cli FLUSHDB for canary namespace only (be careful)
- notify legal/security if PII exposure suspected
maya: adding a small snippet for eval command we use in canary triage:
```
python tools/eval_harness.py --model model-v1.15 --prompt-set canary-prompts.json --threshold 0.86
``` 
carol: thanks all. i'll be standby to help with rollback ops if needed. please add any missing checks to the runbook
sam: final: if abort happens, we'll schedule a hot-fix window after 2h for rollback analysis. if safe, rollforward with fix; otherwise keep pinned and start incident path :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: scheduled: release 2026-03-01T10:12Z. canary cohorts: 1%, 5%, 25%, 100%. preflight done. good luck! :rocket:
